chunks: Aban narrated from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
That he was asked about al-Hasbah, so he said:
"My father عليه السلام would stop briefly at al-Abtah, then enter the houses without sleeping at al-Abtah."
So I said to him: "What do you think about one who hastened in two days?"
Is al-Hasbah required of him? He said: "No."

key_terms.الْأَبْطَحَ: al-Abtah, the place associated with this post-hajj stop
key_terms.الْحَصْبَةِ: the stop or stay at al-Abtah after completing the hajj rites
key_terms.تَعَجَّلَ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ: departed early after two days in Mina
key_terms.لَا: a clear negation indicating that it is not required
key_terms.يُحَصِّبَ: to perform al-Hasbah, meaning to stop at al-Abtah

ai.seo_question: Is staying at al-Abtah after hajj obligatory for someone who departs in two days?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of al-Hasbah, the stop at al-Abtah after the rites of hajj. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام states that his father عليه السلام would only stop there briefly without sleeping, and he explicitly rules that one who hastens departure in two days is not required to perform al-Hasbah.
